# Chronological account: the `pi-playdate` build trajectory

## Setup

The session opens with model `synthetic/hf:zai-org/GLM-5.1`, switches to `anthropic/claude-opus-4-6` (msg #3), and runs under that model for the great majority of the work; near the very end (msg #1033, `14:54`) it switches to `openai-codex/gpt-5.4`.

The user's first message (#5) pastes a full spec: build a pi coding-agent extension `pi-playdate` exposing typed `playdate_*` tools for developing Playdate games. The spec includes an explicit verification requirement: *"After each tool works end-to-end, verify by installing locally (`pi install ./pi-playdate`) and driving it from a fresh pi session."*

## Phase 1 — Research, then a single large upfront build

The agent reads the `pi-extension` skill, the template repo's existing files, and reference extensions (`pi-processes`, `pi-ts-aperture`, `pi-obsidian`) to learn the API surface (#6–#85). It resolves where symbols live: `StringEnum` from `@mariozechner/pi-ai`; `truncateTail`/`withFileMutationQueue` from `@mariozechner/pi-coding-agent`; `pi.exec` signature.

It then writes the whole extension in one sweep (#86–#181): `package.json`, `config.ts`, `lib/` (state, exec, sdk, project, pdc, cmake, sim, device), all tools (doctor, build, run_sim, stop_sim, sim_log, screenshot, run_device, new_project), command files, `index.ts`, plus the `skills/playdate/` SKILL.md and reference docs. During this sweep it catches a couple of its own rule violations (inline `await import` in `project.ts` #98 and `cmake.ts` #104) and fixes them.

Notably, the skill reference templates (lua-api, templates) were written from the *prompt's hardcoded examples*, not from any verified SDK source at this point.

## Phase 2 — A long type/lint remediation loop, verified only by `tsc`/`biome`

From #196 onward, the agent's verification mechanism is `pnpm typecheck` / `pnpm lint` / `pnpm format`. The first typecheck (#197) surfaces a cascade:

- Typebox `TS2769` / `[Kind]` overload errors on `Type.Object(...)`.
- `ImageContent` was written in the Anthropic `source` shape; the real type is `{type:"image", data, mimeType}` (#207).
- `setWidget` expects `string[]`, not `string`.
- `ToolCallHeader.optionArgs` expects `{label, value}[]`, not plain strings.

The agent spawns one `worker` (#182) to fix `optionArgs`/`ToolFooter` in `doctor.ts`; the worker replies that **no changes are needed** (#183). The agent accepts this and proceeds to hand-fix the other tool files itself.

It investigates the typebox `[Kind]` mismatch (#218–#299), confirming `pi-processes` typechecks fine with typebox in `dependencies`. The user interjects: **"just use typebox only"** (#239). The agent moves `@sinclair/typebox` from `peerDependencies` to `dependencies` and drops the peer-meta entry.

The user then asks to use the latest `pi-utils-ui` (#246). Bumping versions and editing `package.json` repeatedly breaks JSON parsing via trailing commas (#253, #259) — fixed across two more edits before `pnpm install` succeeds (#265).

## Phase 3 — User-driven redirections on design

- **#278:** "prompt guidelines… need to mention the tool name" and "for the new project, let's not have a command… have this be a skill." The agent deletes `new_project.ts`, removes it from the index, and rewrites every tool's `promptGuidelines` to name its tool.
- **#297:** "where did you get the templates from?" The agent admits they came from the prompt, unverified. After the SDK site times out repeatedly (#202, #328, #421), the user points out the SDK is installed locally (#302). The agent finds it at `~/Developer/PlaydateSDK/` (3.0.5) and re-derives the Lua/C templates from the real `Examples/Game Template/` and `C_API/Examples/Hello World/` directories (#306–#463), rewriting the reference docs to cite their SDK provenance.

Typecheck and lint pass again (#368, and later clean runs).

## Phase 4 — The critical gap: runtime bugs found only by the user's separate session

At #478 the user supplies a separate session log (a "tictactoe" game built in another directory using the installed extension) and says: *"read this session and look at the issues we're having."* The `read_session` result (#480) enumerates four runtime defects that the agent's own `tsc`/`biome` verification never caught:

1. **`playdate_build`** reports "Build failed with 0 error(s)" — a false negative when `pdc` exits non-zero with no parsed diagnostics.
2. **Simulator process management** — the PID was being captured from the macOS `open -a` helper, not the simulator, so tracking broke.
3. **`playdate_screenshot`** — says "simulator not running" when it is.
4. **`playdate_sim_log`** — returns empty while the simulator is running.

The agent reads the tool sources, runs an `oracle` analysis (#487–#488), and confirms the SDK docs via the local HTML. Fixes follow: launch the simulator binary directly (`Playdate Simulator.app/Contents/MacOS/Playdate Simulator`) instead of via `open -a`; add an `exitCode` + synthetic fallback error in `pdc.ts`; rework sim PID tracking, log ring buffer, and reuse detection.

## Phase 5 — Screenshot and simulator-control investigation

The screenshot path goes through several iterations: an osascript window-ID lookup returns `"missing value"` (broken), replaced by a Swift `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` + `screencapture -l <id>` approach (verified by reading a captured PNG, #581), which the user later asks to drop as unreliable (#"probably drop the fallback using osascript").

The user repeatedly asks whether the SDK offers a way to screenshot and control input (#"is there anything in the sdk that helps"). This leads to the DAP discovery: the Playdate Simulator runs a Debug Adapter Protocol server on TCP **55934** (Lua only), using `Content-Length` framing with `initialize`/`evaluate`. The agent proves manual control with standalone python scripts — eval, button input via `playdate.AButtonDown()`, and screenshots via `playdate.simulator.writeToFile()` / `getDisplayImage()` (verified by reading the resulting PNGs).

The user directs: build a real DAP **client inside the extension** and use it for all operations (#"we need to have a dap client(?) in the extension"). A `worker` implements `lib/dap.ts` (`DapClient` over `node:net`, framing, pending-request map with timeout, auto-injected `__pd_inspect()` Lua serializer) plus `sim_input.ts` / `sim_eval.ts` tools. **This DAP client and its tools were validated only by `pnpm typecheck` / `pnpm lint`** — never by `pi install` + a fresh driven session.

Subsequent user instructions are applied: abstract the DAP client so "the agent shouldn't have to run anything" (lazy `ensureSimulatorDap()`), ensure the `AbortSignal` is actually threaded through (#"it seems like you skip it"), and serialize parallel tool calls. For the last, the user proposes `withFileMutationQueue` with a dummy key; the agent implements a sentinel `DAP_QUEUE_KEY` so parallel `playdate_sim_input` calls queue in order (#"Running multiple times the button tap might not work… tool calls are done in parallel").

During this phase the agent also diagnoses two issues as *game* bugs rather than tool bugs: a `main.lua:63 attempt to index a nil value (local 'line')` crash in the tictactoe game (#872), and a clean-build "Couldn't create folder at tictactoe.pdx" caused by the simulator holding the `.pdx` bundle open (#907).

## Phase 6 — Docs, history squash

The agent updates `AGENTS.md` and `SKILL.md` to document DAP serialization (#1010–#1016); the user says the skill update isn't needed (#1021), so it's reverted, keeping only the `AGENTS.md` note. The user then asks to collapse git history into one commit (#1027); the agent deletes `.git`, re-inits, makes a single root commit `8ba91d1` (51 files, 9411 insertions), re-adds the remote, and force-pushes (#1028–#1032).

## Phase 7 — Final investigation (incomplete at transcript end)

Model switches to `gpt-5.4`. The user asks whether tools can trigger the menu, lock, crank, and accelerometer (#1034). The agent searches the SDK, the simulator binary strings, and external integrations. It first answers that crank/accel/menu/lock probably can't be done generically (#1040, #1042), the user pushes back twice (#1041 "that makes no sense", #1043 "are you sure? … figure it out"), and the agent then finds stronger evidence: binary command strings `changecrank %f`, `dockcrank 0/1`, `accel %i %i %i`, `autolock`, `setAutoLockDisabled`; `DebugAdapter*` symbols; and documented simulator keyboard shortcuts (Escape = menu, Cmd/Ctrl-L = lock, `[`/`]` = crank). The transcript **ends mid-investigation at #1064** with these findings presented but **no working mechanism confirmed or implemented**.

## Observable through-line

- The spec's end-to-end verification step — `pi install ./pi-playdate` then driving it from a fresh pi session — was **never performed by the agent at any point**. Its self-verification throughout was limited to `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, and `pnpm format`, plus ad-hoc manual python/bash DAP probes run outside the installed extension.
- Every one of the four concrete runtime defects (build false negative, sim PID tracking, screenshot "not running", empty log) was surfaced by the **user's separate tictactoe session (#478)**, not by the agent's own testing.
- One delegated `worker` (#182) declined to make a requested change, and the lead accepted that and moved on.

I am stopping at the factual account as instructed and have not diagnosed, labeled, or classified the failure, and did not open any taxonomy materials.

## Goal
Build a Pi coding agent extension called `pi-playdate` that lets an agent develop Playdate games using the Playdate SDK. All Playdate operations go through typed `playdate_*` tools (no direct shell-outs to `pdc`, `pdutil`, `cmake`).

## Constraints & Preferences
- No bash pass-through; every Playdate action is a typed tool
- UI (`ctx.ui.*`) is for humans; tool results (structured `details`) are for the LLM
- Device deployment requires `ctx.ui.confirm` every time
- Simulator is the default runtime target
- Cross-platform (macOS primary, Linux/Windows stubs)
- Use `@aliou/pi-utils-settings` for all config (no custom JSON reader/writer)
- Use `@aliou/pi-utils-ui` (latest `^0.2.0`) for tool rendering
- Use `@sinclair/typebox` directly (in `dependencies`, not just peerDeps)
- `promptGuidelines` must mention the tool name since they're added to system prompt without context
- **No `playdate_new_project` tool** — project scaffolding is skill-driven (agent reads template references and uses `write` tool)
- User dislikes hardcoded Lua/C template strings in tool code
- Template content in reference files must be verified against actual SDK docs

- [x] Package.json with correct deps, bundledDependencies, peerDeps (`"*"` range), pi manifest

- [x] `src/lib/exec.ts` — thin wrapper around `pi.exec`
- [x] `src/lib/sdk.ts` — SDK path resolution, version reading, pdc/simulator/ARM toolchain discovery
- [x] `src/lib/project.ts` — project kind detection (lua/c/hybrid), pdxinfo, source/output dirs
- [x] `src/lib/pdc.ts` — run pdc, parse diagnostics
- [x] `src/lib/cmake.ts` — CMake configure+build, parse gcc diagnostics
- [x] `src/lib/sim.ts` — spawn/ki

# Chronological account: the `pi-playdate` build trajectory

## Setup

The session opens with model `synthetic/hf:zai-org/GLM-5.1`, switches to `anthropic/claude-opus-4-6` (msg #3), and runs under that model for the great majority of the work; near the very end (msg #1033, `14:54`) it switches to `openai-codex/gpt-5.4`.

The user's first message (#5) pastes a full spec: build a pi coding-agent extension `pi-playdate` exposing typed `playdate_*` tools for developing Playdate games. The spec includes an explicit verification requirement: *"After each tool works end-to-end, verify by installing locally (`pi install ./pi-playdate`) and driving it from a fresh pi session."*

## Phase 1 — Research, then a single large upfront build

The agent reads the `pi-extension` skill, the template repo's existing files, and reference extensions (`pi-processes`, `pi-ts-aperture`, `pi-obsidian`) to learn the API surface (#6–#85). It resolves where symbols live: `StringEnum` from `@mariozechner/pi-ai`; `truncateTail`/`withFileMutationQueue` from `@mariozechner/pi-coding-agent`; `pi.exec` signature.

It then writes the whole extension in one sweep (#86–#181): `package.json`, `config.ts`, `lib/` (state, exec, sdk, project, pdc, cmake, sim, device), all tools (doctor, build, run_sim, stop_sim, sim_log, screenshot, run_device, new_project), command files, `index.ts`, plus the `skills/playdate/` SKILL.md and reference docs. During this sweep it catches a couple of its own rule violations (inline `await import` in `project.ts` #98 and `cmake.ts` #104) and fixes them.

Notably, the skill reference templates (lua-api, templates) were written from the *prompt's hardcoded examples*, not from any verified SDK source at this point.

## Phase 2 — A long type/lint remediation loop, verified only by `tsc`/`biome`

From #196 onward, the agent's verification mechanism is `pnpm typecheck` / `pnpm lint` / `pnpm format`. The first typecheck (#197) surfaces a cascade:

- Typebox `TS2769` / `[Kind]` overload errors on `Type.Object(...)`.
- `ImageContent` was written in the Anthropic `source` shape; the real type is `{type:"image", data, mimeType}` (#207).
- `setWidget` expects `string[]`, not `string`.
- `ToolCallHeader.optionArgs` expects `{label, value}[]`, not plain strings.

The agent spawns one `worker` (#182) to fix `optionArgs`/`ToolFooter` in `doctor.ts`; the worker replies that **no changes are needed** (#183). The agent accepts this and proceeds to hand-fix the other tool files itself.

It investigates the typebox `[Kind]` mismatch (#218–#299), confirming `pi-processes` typechecks fine with typebox in `dependencies`. The user interjects: **"just use typebox only"** (#239). The agent moves `@sinclair/typebox` from `peerDependencies` to `dependencies` and drops the peer-meta entry.

The user then asks to use the latest `pi-utils-ui` (#246). Bumping versions and editing `package.json` repeatedly breaks JSON parsing via trailing commas (#253, #259) — fixed across two more edits before `pnpm install` succeeds (#265).

## Phase 3 — User-driven redirections on design

- **#278:** "prompt guidelines… need to mention the tool name" and "for the new project, let's not have a command… have this be a skill." The agent deletes `new_project.ts`, removes it from the index, and rewrites every tool's `promptGuidelines` to name its tool.
- **#297:** "where did you get the templates from?" The agent admits they came from the prompt, unverified. After the SDK site times out repeatedly (#202, #328, #421), the user points out the SDK is installed locally (#302). The agent finds it at `~/Developer/PlaydateSDK/` (3.0.5) and re-derives the Lua/C templates from the real `Examples/Game Template/` and `C_API/Examples/Hello World/` directories (#306–#463), rewriting the reference docs to cite their SDK provenance.
